sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Liath is an Irish hero. More than one figure bears the same name. One came from the race of Nemed. He cut down all the trees on the hill of Tara so that grain could grow there. They named the hill Druin Léith after him. The other Liath loved a woman named Brí. Their deaths kept the two from wedding, and the double name Brí Léith marks a great fairy mound of Ireland.

okr.objective: Give the Irish hero Liath and the hill and mound that carry his name.
key_results: Name his race and the clearing of the hill of Tara.
Link him to the great fairy mound Brí Léith.
